syscalls.comment: s390 parameter ordering for clone is different

issue-23: allow clone/unshare when CLONE_NEWUSER (0x10000000) is set, regardless of any other flags combined with it (mask=valueTwo=0x10000000 so only that bit is checked), without requiring CAP_SYS_ADMIN. NOTE: op SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ compares (arg & value) == valueTwo -- value is the mask, valueTwo is the comparison target; omitting valueTwo defaults it to 0 (checks the bit is UNSET), which was an earlier mistake in this profile that silently blocked exactly the case it was meant to allow. Verified live 2026-08-30: without this fix, `clone(...,flags=CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID|SIGCHLD)` returned EPERM even with apparmor=unconfined (pure seccomp block); with this fix, the same call succeeds and bwrap progresses to its next step.

issue-23: allow mount(2) when both MS_REC (0x4000) and MS_SLAVE (0x80000) flags are set (mask=valueTwo=0x84000), i.e. exactly the `mount --make-rslave` remount bwrap performs immediately after entering its new user+mount namespace -- the AppArmor profile in this same directory (coder/security-profiles/apparmor-bwrap-workspace) grants the matching `mount options=(rslave,silent),` rule (note: AppArmor's actual keyword is `rslave`, NOT `make-rslave` -- see BUGFIX #3 in the AppArmor profile for why this distinction mattered and cost several debugging rounds). Verified live 2026-08-30: with this fix and the corrected AppArmor profile (post-BUGFIX #4), `bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --ro-bind / / echo ok` progresses past this step to bwrap's *next* mount(2) call (tmpfs construction) -- see the three additional mount rules below (BUGFIX #5) for what was needed to get past that and every subsequent step.

issue-23 BUGFIX #5 (found live 2026-08-30 via strace -f -e trace=mount against a real, fully-working baseline bwrap run -- see AGENTS.md): allow mount(2) when both MS_NOSUID (0x2) and MS_NODEV (0x4) are set (mask=valueTwo=0x6), i.e. the tmpfs mount bwrap performs for its private /tmp inside the new sandbox root.

issue-23 BUGFIX #5: allow mount(2) when both MS_BIND (0x1000) and MS_REC (0x4000) are set (mask=valueTwo=0x5000=20480), i.e. bwrap's recursive bind-mount construction of its new root (binding `newroot`/`/oldroot` into place). Mask deliberately ignores MS_SILENT and any legacy MS_MGC_VAL bits some libc mount() wrappers OR in (confirmed via strace both variants appear for this same logical step) -- this one rule covers both without needing a separate exact-match rule per variant.

issue-23 BUGFIX #5: allow mount(2) when both MS_REMOUNT (0x20) and MS_BIND (0x1000) are set (mask=valueTwo=0x1020=4128), i.e. the many per-path remount-readonly/noexec bind mounts bwrap performs to lock down /proc, /dev, /sys, and select /etc/* files inside its constructed sandbox root. Mask deliberately ignores MS_RDONLY/MS_NOSUID/MS_NODEV/MS_NOEXEC/MS_SILENT/MS_RELATIME, all of which vary across the ~20 individual remount calls bwrap makes for different target paths -- confirmed via strace this single rule covers every variant observed.

issue-23 BUGFIX #5: allow mount(2) when both MS_REC (0x4000) and MS_PRIVATE (0x40000) are set (mask=valueTwo=0x44000=278528), i.e. bwrap's final oldroot-detach step (`mount --make-rprivate`) immediately before unmounting it. Mask deliberately ignores MS_SILENT. This is the last mount(2) call observed in a complete bwrap invocation via strace against a fully-working (fully-unconfined seccomp+apparmor) baseline run -- these four mount rules together are intended to cover every mount(2) call in that same sequence; live re-verification with all four rules plus the corrected AppArmor profile applied (not yet performed as of authoring this rule) is required before treating Issue #23 as closed.

issue-23 BUGFIX #6 (found live 2026-08-30, re-verifying BUGFIX #5): with all four mount rules above applied and apparmor=unconfined, bwrap progressed past every mount(2) call and failed on a different syscall entirely -- pivot_root(2), returning EPERM. Confirmed via inspecting Docker's own unmodified default seccomp profile (docker inspect --format '{{.HostConfig.SecurityOpt}}' on a plain container): pivot_root is absent from every rule group in Docker's default profile, including the CAP_SYS_ADMIN-gated group that mount/clone/unshare/etc. belong to -- Docker's default profile unconditionally blocks pivot_root for every container regardless of capabilities, presumably an intentionally stricter default given how powerful it is (swaps a process's root filesystem). This is safe to unconditionally allow here because bwrap only calls it after already confining itself inside its own new user+mount namespace (via the CLONE_NEWUSER rule above) -- a pivot_root call at that point can only ever affect that process's own private, already-isolated mount namespace, never the host's real root or any other container's namespace. No argument-based scoping is possible for this rule (pivot_root(2) takes two path arguments, not an inspectable integer flags word the way mount(2) does).

issue-23 BUGFIX #7 (found live 2026-08-30, re-verifying BUGFIX #6): with the pivot_root rule above added, bwrap progressed further and failed on `umount2(2)` ("unmount old root": Operation not permitted). `umount`/`umount2` are both grouped in Docker's default profile's *same* CAP_SYS_ADMIN-gated rule as `mount`/`clone`/`unshare` -- Docker's seccomp profile GENERATOR evaluates that `includes.caps` condition once, at container-create time, against the container's assigned capability set (not dynamically per-syscall against the calling process's live/namespaced capability state) -- since these containers are never granted CAP_SYS_ADMIN in their outer capability set (by design, matching this whole issue's constraint), that gated rule is compiled out of the final BPF filter entirely for them, exactly like `mount` was before BUGFIX #5's dedicated rules. Same justification as pivot_root above: safe to unconditionally allow because bwrap only unmounts its own already-namespace-isolated `/oldroot`, not anything reachable outside its own mount namespace.

issue-23 BUGFIX #8 (found live 2026-08-30, first found against a *real* Coder workspace running `srt opencode`, not just a synthetic `bwrap --ro-bind / /` test): `srt` invokes `bwrap` with `--dev /dev` (to provide a fresh, isolated `/dev` including a pty), which the minimal reproduction command used through BUGFIX #7 never exercised. `strace -f -e trace=mount` against `bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --dev /dev --ro-bind / /` (matching srt's real invocation shape) found one more distinct mount(2) call: `mount("devpts", "/newroot/dev/pts", "devpts", MS_NOSUID|MS_NOEXEC, "newinstance,ptmxmode=0666,mode=...")` -- allow mount(2) when both MS_NOSUID (0x2) and MS_NOEXEC (0x8) are set (mask=valueTwo=0xa=10).
